predecessors.name: Spanish Empire
predecessors.text: the Captaincy General of Santo Domingo, eastern Hispaniola: the state 'succeeded the Captaincy General of Santo Domingo after independence was declared'

successors.name: Haiti
successors.text: the eastern part of the island: 'On 9 February 1822, Boyer formally entered the capital city'

ledger.x: 1 December 1821: Núñez de Cáceres declares the independence of Spanish Haiti at Santo Domingo.
13 December 1821: Puerto Plata raises the Haitian flag.
15 December 1821: Dajabón raises the Haitian flag on the frontier with Haiti.
29 December 1821: Santiago raises the Haitian flag.
4 January 1822: La Vega raises the Haitian flag; 'the people began to raise the Haitian flag on public buildings and plazas.'
February 1822: Spanish Haiti ends in the Haitian occupation.

wars.name: Haitian occupation of Santo Domingo (1822)
wars.outcome: Haitian annexation without a battle: towns raise the Haitian flag from 13 December 1821 and Boyer enters Santo Domingo on 9 February 1822.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary text for the frontier with Haiti; the island is shown as the former Captaincy General of Santo Domingo.
